| Item | The common description of INFP |
| --- | --- |
| Four preferences | Introverted I, Intuitive N, Feeling F, Perceiving P |
| Attention and energy (I) | Attention tends to turn inward, toward ideas and reflection. |
| Information (N) | Patterns, connections and possibilities carry more weight when taking in information. |
| Decision criteria (F) | Values and the effects on people carry more weight when making decisions. |
| Approach to the outside world (P) | Keep options open for new information. A deadline can still be firm. |
| Function stack | Dominant Fi, auxiliary Ne, tertiary Si and inferior Te in this convention. The tertiary orientation varies by source. |
| A/T suffix | The NERIS Identity from 16Personalities, not a fifth official MBTI dimension |
| Sample share | 4.4% of the US Form M manual sample (132 of 3,009), per the [manual column in Table 5 of Erford et al. (2025)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcad.70006) |

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
The letters cover four questions about attention, information, decision criteria and the approach to the outside world.

Introversion describes attention and energy tending toward inner thoughts and experience. Someone can speak readily in a meeting and still prefer reflecting privately. Speaking style alone cannot establish I or E.

Intuition gives more weight to patterns and possibilities. Two readers of the same story might notice different things: what the character could have done or what the character actually said. Either reader can consider both.

Feeling gives weight to values and the people affected. When planning an event, a team can check who would have trouble signing up and compare the costs of the options. Both considerations can inform the same decision.

Perceiving describes an outward preference for taking in information and leaving room to adjust. Someone can keep a firm deadline while deciding what to include. The date they make a decision does not establish J or P.

“Mediator” is a label used by 16Personalities. Whether someone wants to help resolve a disagreement depends on their role, experience and choice.

### The Fi–Ne–Si–Te four-function notation used here

In type dynamics, I places the dominant process inward. P identifies the outward process as perceiving. For INFP, N makes that auxiliary extraverted Intuition (Ne), while F points to dominant introverted Feeling (Fi). This page uses Si for tertiary Sensing and Te for inferior Thinking.

Within the model, Fi weighs choices against personal values. Ne explores connections and possibilities. Si draws on remembered details and experience. Te uses external criteria to organise decisions. No fixed sequence follows from the stack.

In a fictional club, one writer starts with a principle: describe newcomers as people making their own choices. Another discovers the same priority after drafting an invitation. Either sequence can serve the same goal.

The [Foundation’s type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/) lists tertiary Sensing as Se or Si for INFP. This page uses Si. The dominant and auxiliary descriptions remain the same.
sections.title: INFP letters and framework

sections.body_md:
Separate the principle you want to preserve from the methods you can change. That helps you see which feedback you can act on without changing the purpose of the work.

In a fictional exhibition, the team wants visitors to hear the makers’ stories but the long labels make it hard to find a starting point. A short opening note can point visitors to one work and explain why. The longer accounts can stay in a separate guide.

| Situation | Consideration | Possible cost | What to try |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Setting a theme | Decide whose needs the piece should serve | One piece can take on too many goals | Name one reader and one goal |
| Finding a way to present it | Consider several ways to tell the story | Reworking the draft can crowd out reader feedback | Share the clearest version with a reader |
| Hearing disagreement | Ask whether the criticism affects a principle you want to preserve | A comment on style can feel like a personal judgment | Ask which sentence caused the issue and how |
| Revisiting an agreement | Name the value you want to preserve | Others may miss an unspoken concern | Say what concerns you and which methods can change |
| Finishing a draft | Keep the voice the piece needs | The result may fall short of the version you imagined | Agree on what a deliverable version must contain |

Someone who likes exploring options can still follow a strict proofreading checklist. A writer can use a proven format when a budget rules out other options. Note which choices were possible before drawing conclusions about someone’s preferences.
sections.title: INFP traits, strengths and blind spots

sections.body_md:
Start with a task you would be willing to repeat. Then check how feedback arrives, how much autonomy you have and what the role does on an ordinary day.

An editor can care about a charity’s work and still spend most of the day checking facts, clarifying wording and meeting deadlines. Separate your interest in the subject from your interest in doing the work regularly.

| Activity to explore | What you can try | Career profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interviews and questionnaires | Turn a broad question into two that people can answer without guessing what you mean. Pilot them on a small fictional topic. | [Survey researchers](/en/career/jobs/survey-researchers) |
| Needs and feedback | Use two public or fictional interview extracts. Compare why each respondent chose the same product, and mark what is still uncertain. | [Market research analysts](/en/career/jobs/market-research-analysts) |

Consider which stage you would repeat: interviewing, analysing evidence, revising or writing. Ask who makes the final edit, what feedback the team gives and how much discretion the role allows. If the subject is the main attraction, compare other roles in the same field.
sections.title: INFP work and career exploration

sections.body_md:
When people hear the same words differently, make the request specific enough for the other person to respond.

In a fictional example, a friend repeats a private remark as a joke. You might say, “I’m happy to talk about that with you privately. Please don’t share it with other people.” Ask whether the boundary is clear.

If you need time to yourself, say when you can reconnect and what will happen to plans you already made. For example: “I need some quiet time until eight. I’ll call after that.”

After a difficult conversation, each person can restate what they understood and invite the other to correct it.
sections.title: INFP relationships and communication

sections.body_md:
If a task feels difficult, ask whether you disagree with the goal or need a different way to carry it out. A disagreement about the goal needs a conversation. A problem with time or resources may need a smaller task or more support.

In a fictional event, the budget for requested live captions falls short. Ask attendees who rely on captions what would give them access. Discuss options with them and describe what will actually be available before they decide whether to attend. Check applicable accessibility requirements with the organiser.

If interruptions are the problem, choose the task that needs attention today and tell anyone affected which deadlines will move. If poor sleep, low mood or distress persists or disrupts daily life, consider speaking with a qualified professional.
sections.title: INFP stress and recovery

sections.body_md:
Record what mattered to you, what you tried and what evidence showed whether it worked.

As a fictional exercise, write two versions of an event notice. Ask a willing reader to explain what to do, by when and what to bring. Revise one unclear point and check it again. A clear answer shows what the reader understood.

Include an occasion when you followed an established process even though you had other ideas. Note what the task required and where you had room to choose.

Stop if the notes only prompt you to look for a label. Use the exercise to understand a decision you can revisit.
sections.title: INFP observation practice

sections.body_md:
These related pages each change one letter. They can help you see what each preference pair describes.

### INFP against its neighbours on the preference axes

| Neighbouring type | Shared letters | Actual difference | What each may focus on in one scene |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [INFJ and INFP compared](/en/personality/infj-vs-infp) | I, N, F | J/P: settling an outward arrangement or keeping options open | With the same available information, which part of a plan would you settle now? |
| [ISFP and INFP compared](/en/personality/isfp-vs-infp) | I, F, P | S/N: concrete observations and experience or patterns and possibilities | Looking at the same exhibit, which draws attention: its observable details or connections and possibilities? |
| [ENFP profile](/en/personality/enfp) | N, F, P | E/I: orientation toward the outer or inner world | When an idea needs work and you have time, does discussion or private reflection draw your attention more naturally? |

Someone of either type in each comparison can take either approach. If you see A or T after INFP, those suffixes refer to 16Personalities’ Identity aspect.

- [What the INFP-A suffix means](/en/personality/infp-a)
- [What the INFP-T suffix means](/en/personality/infp-t)
- [INFP-A and INFP-T compared](/en/personality/infp-a-vs-infp-t)
- [Browse the personality directory](/en/personality)

sections.body_md:
**Framework sources.** See the [Myers & Briggs Foundation’s type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/) for the functions. The [manual column in Table 5 of Erford et al. (2025)](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jcad.70006) reports the U.S. Form M manual sample as a benchmark. The authors excluded studies presented in the manuals from their analyses to preserve sample independence.

**Function-stack convention.** This page uses Fi–Ne–Si–Te. The Foundation’s overview also allows Se for tertiary Sensing. These positions describe the model and cannot predict ability, career fit or how people will work together.

**Editorial fiction.** The club notice, exhibition, career exercises, private conversation, event and notice test are fictional examples. They illustrate trade-offs without describing any real person or organisation.

**Scope.** This page is for reflection. Assessment results are unsuitable for hiring, ranking ability or predicting relationships. The Form M sample figure describes one group. FermatMind uses its own questions and scoring. See the [assessment method and evidence statement](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

FermatMind Editorial

sections.body_md:

sections.body_md:

| Decision criteria (F) | Values and the effects on people carry more weight when making decisions. |
